name: Benign Infantile Focal Epilepsy with Midline Spikes and Waves During Sleep
aliases: Benign Infantile Focal Epilepsy with Midline Spikes
Benign Infantile Epilepsy with Sleep-Related Midline Spikes

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Benign Infantile Focal Epilepsy Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Onset of focal seizures in infancy with preserved normal development
EEG showing midline spikes and waves predominantly during sleep
Normal brain MRI without structural abnormalities
Spontaneous remission of seizures by 2 years of age without neurological sequelae

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of typical focal seizures in infancy, EEG with midline spikes and waves during sleep, and benign clinical course with normal development
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of symptomatic epilepsies and structural brain lesions

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal seizures with unilateral clonic movements
pathognomonic.notes: Typically brief and occur during wakefulness
searchTerms: focal seizures causing unilateral clonic activity
jerking on one side during seizures

pathognomonic.symptomName: Midline spikes and waves on EEG during non-REM sleep
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic EEG pattern essential for diagnosis
searchTerms: spike and wave patterns in middle brain region during sleep
EEG midline spikes in non-REM sleep

pathognomonic.notes: No cognitive or motor delay observed

common.notes: Seizures often occur in clusters, especially during sleep
Involuntary twitching localized to one side of the face
searchTerms: brief twitching on one side of face
quick facial twitches on one side

common.notes: Seizures usually do not impair awareness
searchTerms: no loss of awareness during seizures

common.notes: No focal neurological deficits between seizures
searchTerms: no signs of neurological problems interictally
neurological exam normal when not seizing

occasional.notes: Brief period of drowsiness following seizures
Rare progression to generalized tonic-clonic seizures
searchTerms: seizures sometimes spread to whole body

occasional.notes: Transient behavioral changes during frequent seizures
searchTerms: slight mood changes with seizure groups
short episodes of pale or blue skin during seizures
brief autonomic symptoms like pallor or cyanosis

rare.notes: History of febrile seizures in infancy
searchTerms: seizures triggered by fever early on

rare.symptomName: Transient developmental delay during seizure clusters
rare.notes: Temporary mild delay that resolves after remission
searchTerms: temporary developmental slowdown during seizure clusters
transient delay in skills with seizure groups

rare.symptomName: Sleep disruption due to nocturnal seizures
searchTerms: sleep problems caused by nighttime seizures
disrupted sleep due to seizures at night

laboratory: Normal metabolic and biochemical blood tests
imaging: Normal brain MRI without structural abnormalities
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; familial cases rare
other: Characteristic EEG pattern with midline spikes and waves during sleep

distinguishingFeatures: EEG shows centrotemporal spikes rather than midline spikes
Seizures often occur during wakefulness rather than sleep

references: Specchio N, et al. Benign infantile focal epilepsy with midline spikes and waves during sleep: clinical and EEG features. Epilepsia. 2015.
Berg AT, et al. Classification of epilepsies and epileptic syndromes. Epilepsia. 2010.
